newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says no Arafat offer to help end war.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says no Arafat offer to help end war.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Tuesday it had received no formal offer from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to help end the island's 13-year-old ethnic war.
"No formal offer has been made by President Arafat to the government of Sri Lanka," Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar told a news conference in Colombo with Arafat sitting next to him.
"I am at your disposal and put all my efforts to help achieve a settlement," Arafat told a public meeting on Monday.
"I am making the offer officially now," he said.

"As a friend of Sri Lanka President Arafat would like to see peace return to our land. He is a man who has known both war and peace. He also knows how difficult it is to achieve peace and to keep the peace," Kadirgamar told the news conference.

"If impossible demands are not made, peace will come and negotiations can take place," he added in reference to the war over the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels' demand for a separate homeland in the island's north and east for minority Tamils.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE says the number is higher.
Arafat said the Sri Lankan rebels should start considering the peace option to end ethnic strife in the island.
"They will have to follow the line of peace," he said.
"LTTE is different," Arafat said when asked whether he saw any similarity between them and the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
The Sri Lankan government in the past has declined all offers for third party mediation to end the war, saying it was the island's internal matter.
